options: A reaction that releases energy to its surroundings
A reaction that absorbs energy from its surroundings
A reaction with no energy change
A reaction that only happens in space
questions.explanation: An exothermic reaction releases energy — exo (out) + therm (heat), so energy flows outward.
questions.misconception: Absorbing energy is the endothermic reaction's job — the exothermic reaction is specifically the one that RELEASES energy outward.

questions.prompt: In what form does an exothermic reaction usually release its energy?
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions release energy mainly as heat, and sometimes as light — like a flame's glow.
questions.misconception: The classic exothermic output is heat and light (think fire) — not sound, electricity, or stored energy.

questions.prompt: Why does an exothermic reaction release energy?
options: The reactants hold more energy than the products — the extra is released
The products hold more energy than the reactants
Energy is created out of nowhere
questions.explanation: In an exothermic reaction the reactants start with more energy; when they form lower-energy products, the difference escapes outward.
questions.misconception: Energy is never created and atoms are never lost — the release happens because the products are lower-energy, not because anything new appears.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an exothermic reaction?
options: A hand warmer heating up when cracked
questions.explanation: A hand warmer releasing heat is a classic exothermic reaction — it gives energy out, warming your hands.
questions.misconception: Cold packs, melting ice, and absorbing sunlight all take energy IN — those are the endothermic pattern. The hand warmer gives energy OUT.
